blocks.prompt: 6 Prove that: \(\dfrac{\sin 3\theta}{1 + 2\cos 2\theta} = \sin\theta\); deduce the value of \(\sin 15^{\circ}\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein do kaam hain: pehle identity saabit karni hai, phir usi ko ek khaas angle par laga kar \(\sin 15^{\circ}\) nikalna hai.
Asal chaal: \(\sin 3\theta\) ko \(\sin\theta + (\sin 3\theta - \sin\theta)\) likh dein. Bracket "sin − sin" hai jo \(2\cos 2\theta\sin\theta\) ban jata hai, aur phir \(\sin\theta\) common nikal aata hai.
Plan: \(\sin 3\theta = \sin\theta(1 + 2\cos 2\theta)\) dikhayein, divide karein, phir \(\theta = 15^{\circ}\) rakh kar rationalise karein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin 3\theta}{1 + 2\cos 2\theta}\).
Saabit karna hai: L.H.S. \(= \sin\theta\); phir \(\sin 15^{\circ}\) nikalna hai.
Tareeqa: Numerator ko factorise karne ke liye \(\sin P - \sin Q = 2\cos\frac{P + Q}{2}\sin\frac{P - Q}{2}\).

Numerator ko torein
\[\sin 3\theta = \sin\theta + (\sin 3\theta - \sin\theta)\]
Kyun: \(\sin\theta\) jama bhi kiya aur minus bhi, to value wohi rahi. Lekin ab bracket mein sines ka farq ban gaya jis par formula lag sakta hai. Yeh "jama-tafreeq" wali trick bohat kaam ki hai.

Bracket ko product banayein
\[\sin 3\theta - \sin\theta = 2\cos 2\theta\sin\theta\]
Kyun: Aadha jama \(\frac{3\theta + \theta}{2} = 2\theta\) cosine mein, aadha farq \(\frac{3\theta - \theta}{2} = \theta\) sine mein.

Factorise karein
\[\sin 3\theta = \sin\theta + 2\cos 2\theta\sin\theta\]
\[= \sin\theta(1 + 2\cos 2\theta)\]
Kyun: Dono terms mein \(\sin\theta\) hai, bahar nikal liya. Dekhein, bracket bilkul denominator jaisa ban gaya.

Divide karein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \dfrac{\sin\theta(1 + 2\cos 2\theta)}{1 + 2\cos 2\theta}\]
\[= \sin\theta = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Kyun: \(1 + 2\cos 2\theta\) upar neeche cancel (yeh zero nahi hona chahiye, warna fraction ka matlab hi nahi banta).

Natija (deduction): \(\theta = 15^{\circ}\) rakhein
\[\sin 15^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sin 45^{\circ}}{1 + 2\cos 30^{\circ}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{1 + 2\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}(1 + \sqrt{3})}\]
Kyun: \(\theta = 15^{\circ}\) is liye chuna ke \(3\theta = 45^{\circ}\) aur \(2\theta = 30^{\circ}\) ban jayen, jin ki values hum jaante hain. Identity har angle ke liye sahi hai, is liye \(15^{\circ}\) par bhi.

Denominator ko rationalise karein
\[\sin 15^{\circ} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{2}(\sqrt{3} + 1)(\sqrt{3} - 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{\sqrt{2}(3 - 1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{3} - 1}{2\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: Neeche \(\sqrt{3} + 1\) hai; upar neeche \(\sqrt{3} - 1\) se multiply karne par \((a + b)(a - b) = a^2 - b^2\) se \(3 - 1 = 2\) ban jata hai aur surd khatam.
Dhyan dein: Sirf neeche multiply kar dena ghalat hai; upar bhi wohi factor lagana zaroori hai.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{1.7321 - 1}{2.8284} \approx 0.2588\]
\[\sin 15^{\circ} \approx 0.2588 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Calculator wali value se milta hai. Exercise 10.2 mein \(\sin(45^{\circ} - 30^{\circ})\) se bhi yahi jawab aaya tha, to do alag raaston se ek hi manzil.
